criteria: reads applicable AGENTS.md and openspec/project-context.md before governed work
uses accepted specs, active changes, ADRs, and Git as scoped authorities without creating handoff files
classifies changes as direct or standard and upgrades ambiguity to standard
reconciles tasks with code, diffs, commits, and fresh verification after compaction or in a new session
queries archive and Git history only when current facts do not answer a relevant question

cases.prompt: Use $govern-openspec-context at {skill_path} to initialize {repo_path} for durable OpenSpec project context. Preview first, then apply. Do not edit AGENTS.md.
expected: creates project-context but no handoff or custom schema

cases.prompt: Use $govern-openspec-context at {skill_path} in {repo_path}. Fix the misspelling in the internal comment and verify the edit.
expected: does not create an OpenSpec change

cases.prompt: Use $govern-openspec-context at {skill_path} in {repo_path}. Continue the active change after conversation compaction and implement the next evidence-supported task.
expected: rereads project context and active artifacts
reconciles tasks with Git diff and code
does not create a handoff or checkpoint file

cases.prompt: Use $govern-openspec-context at {skill_path} in {repo_path}. Resume the only active OpenSpec change and report the next dependency-ready task.
expected: checks task claims against repository evidence

cases.prompt: Use $govern-openspec-context at {skill_path} in {repo_path}. Resume the relevant active OpenSpec change.
expected: does not guess between indistinguishable candidates
asks for an exact change ID

cases.prompt: Use $govern-openspec-context at {skill_path} in {repo_path}. Explain why the public output format uses version 2.
expected: reads current context and spec first
consults focused archive or Git history only if needed
